accepted.question_text: Let (K, v) be a tame valued field, meaning equivalently that (K, v) is henselian, algebraically maximal, has perfect residue field Kv, and—when char Kv = p > 0—has p-divisible value group vK. Does there exist a suitable language extending the language of valued rings in which the class of tame fields admits quantifier elimination?

evidence.quote: Open problem 1: Do tame fields admit quantifier elimination in a suitable language?

Theorem 8 (Kuhlmann (2016)). A henselian field (K, v) is a tame field if and only if the following conditions hold: (TF1) if char Kv = p > 0, then vK is p-divisible, (TF2) Kv is perfect, (TF3) (K, v) is algebraically maximal.

accepted.question_text: Consider the maximal immediate extensions of the deeply ramified mixed-characteristic fields Q_p(ζ_{p^∞}) and Q_p(p^{1/p^∞}) discussed in the paper. Beyond the fact that these extensions are infinite, what concrete structural features do they have, and which structural features distinguish the extensions whose elementary theories are decidable from those whose elementary theories are undecidable?

evidence.quote: Open problem 2: What is the structure of these extensions (apart from the fact that they are infinite)? What are the indications in their structure that distinguish the decidable from the undecidable extensions?

Theorem 5 (Kartas (2024)). The fields Qp(ζp∞) and Qp(p1/p∞) equipped with their unique extensions vp of the p-adic valuation admit maximal immediate extensions which have decidable elementary Lval-theories.

accepted.question_text: Are the valued fields Q_p(ζ_{p^∞}), Q_p(p^{1/p^∞}), and Q_p^{ab} decidable in the language of valued rings? Likewise, are the positive-characteristic fields F_p((t))^{1/p^∞} and F_p^{ac}((t))^{1/p^∞} decidable in the language of valued rings, or even in the language of valued rings with a distinguished constant symbol t?

evidence.quote: Open problem 3: Are Qp(ζp∞), Qp(p1/p∞) and Qab p decidable in Lval ? Are Fp((t))1/p∞ and Fac p ((t))1/p∞ decidable in Lval or even Lval(t)?

accepted.question_text: Kartas proves that decidability of F_p((t))^{1/p^∞} in L_val(t) would imply decidability of Q_p(ζ_{p^∞}) and Q_p(p^{1/p^∞}) in L_val, and that decidability of F_p^{ac}((t))^{1/p^∞} in L_val(t) would imply decidability of Q_p^{ab} in L_val. Does a converse transfer hold in a strong form, ideally recovering decidability on the positive-characteristic side in the language L_val(t)?

evidence.quote: Open problem 4: What about the reverse direction?

Theorem 6 (Kartas (2024)). (a) If Fp((t))1/p∞ has a decidable elementary or existential Lval(t)-theory, then Qp(ζp∞) and Qp(p1/p∞) have decidable elementary or existential Lval-theories, respectively. (b) If Fac p ((t))1/p∞ has a decidable elementary or existential Lval(t)-theory, then Qab p has a decidable elementary or existential Lval-theory, respectively.
So a more precise version of problem 4 is whether this argument can be improved to get decidability in Lval(t) on the positive characteristic side.

accepted.question_text: What model-theoretic description can be given for roughly deeply ramified fields, relative to their value groups and residue fields? In particular, what can be said about the model theory of the perfect hull F_p((t))^{1/p^∞}, which lies naturally in this setting?
accepted.context_brief: Model theory of roughly deeply ramified fields

evidence.quote: Open problem 5: What can we say about the model theory of (roughly) deeply ramified fields (relative to their value groups and residue fields), and in particular of Fp((t))1/p∞ ?

accepted.question_text: Let F_p(t)^h denote the henselization of the rational function field F_p(t) with its t-adic valuation, and let F_p((t)) be the Laurent series field with the same valuation. Is F_p(t)^h an elementary substructure of F_p((t)) in the language of valued rings?

evidence.quote: Open problem 6: Is Fp(t)h an elementary substructure of Fp((t))?

accepted.question_text: Can one prove model-theoretic results for henselian perfect valued fields of positive characteristic that are analogous to the known results for tame fields—such as relative model completeness, completeness, or decidability—perhaps under additional mild hypotheses weaker than tameness?

evidence.quote: Open problem 7: Is it possible to prove model theoretic results for henselian perfect valued fields of positive characteristic, analoguous to those for tame fields (but under mild additional conditions)?

Theorem 1 (Kuhlmann (2016)). Tame fields (K, v) satisfy model completeness in the language Lval of valued rings relative to the elementary theories of their value groups vK in the language of ordered groups and their residue fields Kv in the language of rings. If char K = char Kv, then also relative completeness and relative decidability hold.

accepted.question_text: What is the full model theory of the valued Laurent series field F_p((t))? More specifically, can one find a complete axiomatization of F_p((t)) and determine whether its full elementary theory is decidable?

evidence.quote: Open problem 8: What can we say about the model theory and in particular a complete axiomatization and the decidability of Fp((t))?

accepted.question_text: There exist henselian defectless valued fields of positive characteristic that are not existentially closed in their maximal immediate extensions. Is there a natural and practically usable additional condition on the relevant immediate extensions that restores existential closedness in maximal immediate extensions?

evidence.quote: Open problem 9: Is there a handy additional condition on the immediate extensions that remedies this situation?
Proposition 12 (Kuhlmann (2001)). There are henselian defectless fields that are not Lval-existentially closed in their maximal immediate extensions.

accepted.question_text: Let (A) be the axiom system saying that a valued field is henselian and defectless, has positive characteristic, has value group a Z-group, and has residue field F_p. If one adds the elementary axiom scheme asserting that the field is extremal, does the resulting theory become complete?

evidence.quote: Open problem 10: Is (A) + "(K, v) is extremal" a complete axiom system?
Theorem 13 (Kuhlmann (2001)). The Lval-elementary axiom system (A) "henselian defectless valued field of positive characteristic with value group a Z-group and residue field Fp" is not complete.
A valued field (K, v) is called extremal if for every multi-variable polynomial f(X1, . . . , Xn) over K, the set {v(f(a1, . . . , an)) | a1, . . . , an ∈ OK} ⊆ vK ∪ {∞} has a maximal element.

accepted.question_text: Suppose a valuation v decomposes as a composition v = w ◦ ̄w, where both the coarser valuation w and the induced residue valuation ̄w are extremal, and where the value group of w is divisible. Must the composite valuation v itself be extremal?

evidence.quote: Open problem 11: If v = w◦w¯ with w and ¯w extremal and w has divisible value group, does it follow that v is extremal?

accepted.question_text: Suppose a valuation v decomposes as v = w ◦ ̄w and that v is extremal. It is known that the induced residue valuation ̄w is extremal. Does extremality of v also force the coarser valuation w to be extremal?

evidence.quote: Open problem 12: We know that if v = w ◦ w¯ is extremal, then so is w¯ (see [6, Lemma 4.1]). But does it also follow that w is extremal?

accepted.question_text: Is every extremal valued field existentially closed in each of its maximal immediate extensions?

evidence.quote: Open problem 13: Is every extremal valued field existentially closed in its maximal immediate extensions?

accepted.question_text: Let (R4) denote the statement that every large field K is existentially closed in every extension field F that admits a K-rational place. Does (R4) hold for arbitrary fields?

evidence.quote: Open problem 14: Does (R4) hold?
In the paper [2] the assumption that implication 1)⇒3) holds for arbitrary fields K is called hypothesis (R4).

Theorem 18 (Kuhlmann (2004)). Let K be a perfect field. Then the following conditions are equivalent: 1) K is a large field, 2) K is existentially closed in every power series field K((tΓ)), 3) K is existentially closed in every extension field L which admits a K-rational place.

accepted.question_text: Knaf and Kuhlmann proved local uniformization by alteration. Does this imply a useful alteration-based analogue of (R4), namely a statement strong enough to support a meaningful 'model theory by alteration'?

evidence.quote: Open problem 15: Does local uniformization by alteration imply a reasonable (and useful) hypothesis "(R4) by alteration"? Is there a "model theory by alteration"?
By valuation theoretical tools, Knaf and Kuhlmann proved local uniformization by alteration in [23].

accepted.question_text: Call a henselian valued field (K, v) roughly deeply ramified if it satisfies the axioms (DRvr) and (DRvp) stated in the paper. It is conjectured there that this should be equivalent to the property that all algebraic extensions of (K, v) are independent defect fields. If every algebraic extension of a henselian field (K, v) is an independent defect field, must (K, v) already be roughly deeply ramified?

evidence.quote: In view of Theorem 9, we conjecture that a henselian field is a roughly deeply ramified field if and only if all of its algebraic extensions are independent defect fields. Thus we ask:
Open problem 16: If all algebraic extensions of a henselian field (K, v) are independent defect fields, does it follow that (K, v) is a roughly deeply ramified field?
